sourceFinding: t2 verifier finding L6-F2 (high), evidence/ulw/l6-verification/20260918T012345Z/result.json (sha256 e2407d6a95d489fb1c749a44585db641ec003c5414a51658ab3fd8d49c029a68), output.log line 90 (sha256 7a5999b56b7a82e62345d7191de33a5256544a8b4a055f706067b04fa080c90a)

defect.symptom: every plan=false mpd_ultrawork call failed at the harness output boundary: `Error: tool "mpd_ultrawork" returned invalid output: "value.planFile" must be a string` (quoted verbatim in failing-excerpt.log)
defect.rootCause: the declared output schema said `planFile: { type: "string" }` while the engine returned `planFile: string | null` — null whenever plan=false, which is the /ulw command default
defect.blastRadius: plan=false is the default for the user-invocable /ulw path; mpd_ulw is a compatibility alias over the same engine

designDecision.chosen: OMIT the `planFile` key when it is null (conditional spread in the return), keeping `planFile: { type: "string" }` and leaving it out of `required` — plus a schema `description` stating when it is present.
designDecision.whyNotNullableType: The verifier's requiredFix offered `planFile: { type: ["string","null"] }` as one option. The INSTALLED harness validator does not support type arrays: its own source (dsh-tools/lib/index.js, checkSchemaNode) says `${path}.type must be a single type string (type arrays are not supported)`, and the vendored copy of the same validator REJECTS that schema at author time (measured — see validator-measurement.log). Declaring it would have replaced a value violation with an author-schema violation.

measuredValidator.type: [\"string\",\"null\"]: REJECTED at author level: unsupported JSON schema: … properties.planFile.type must be a single type string

fix.change: the engine's return becomes `{ status, rounds: used, ...(planFile === null ? {} : { planFile }), verdict, ledger: gateLedger, finalReport, stateFile }` (documented in place), and the declared schema's `planFile` gains a description: present only when a plan file was written. No other behaviour changed.
invariants: plan=true still returns the plan path as a string
state.json on disk still records planFile (null when none) — only the TOOL RESULT shape changed
the mpd_ulw alias and the render functions are untouched

mutationControl.purpose: prove the new declared-schema test is falsifiable
mutationControl.result: with the RETIRED unconditional return restored, the suite is 13 pass / 1 fail — the failing test being 'the DECLARED mpd_ultrawork output schema accepts the engine's own plan=false AND plan=true results'; file restored byte-exactly (sha256 1e10df6ef960b4d0c0927d67f26ecebbb30b3870310396997b747a4e5fd9aa37 before and after)

acceptance.criterion: The declared output schema accepts the engine's own plan=false result (planFile null) — either by allowing null for that property or by omitting the key when null — so a plan=false run no longer produces `tool "mpd_ultrawork" returned invalid output: "value.planFile" must be a string`
acceptance.evidence: The engine now omits `planFile` when it is null; the declared schema keeps `planFile: { type: "string" }` (already absent from `required`), so declaration and value agree. Unit proof: the real plan=false result validates with `validateJsonSchemaValue(schema, light) === []` (harness's own validator, imported copy). Live proof: the model-initiated plan=false call recorded `isError=false` and the session log carries 0 occurrences of `returned invalid output` (live/result.json steps.livePlanFalse.invalidOutputHits = 0).

acceptance.criterion: A unit test validates a REAL engine result for plan=false AND for plan=true against the DECLARED schema object (not a hand-written shape and not a copy of it), so the two can never drift apart unnoticed again
acceptance.evidence: 'the DECLARED mpd_ultrawork output schema accepts the engine's own plan=false AND plan=true results' (test/engine.test.ts): takes `tools.find(t => t.name === "mpd_ultrawork").output.schema` — the DECLARED object reference, never a copy — asserts it passes `assertSupportedJsonSchema`, runs the engine for plan=false (asserts the key is ABSENT) and plan=true (asserts a string path), and validates BOTH real results with the harness's own `validateJsonSchemaValue`, expecting []. NEGATIVE CONTROL: the same validator rejects the retired `{...light, planFile: null}` shape with exactly 1 violation naming planFile, so the empty lists are meaningful.

acceptance.criterion: The mpd_ulw alias path (which hardcodes plan=false) is exercised and passes
acceptance.evidence: Unit: 'the mpd_ulw alias path (hardcoded plan=false) is exercised and its result matches its DECLARED schema' executes the alias tool, validates its result against the alias's own declared schema ([]) and asserts the four returned fields' types. Live: the same boot issued a model-initiated mpd_ulw call (`{"objective":"qa-l2c-schema-alias","maxRounds":1}`) whose recorded result is `isError=false`. HONEST NOTE: the alias returns a NARROW object (status/rounds/finalReport/stateFile) and never carried planFile, so its own result was already schema-valid; the DISCRIMINATING path for this defect is mpd_ultrawork with plan=false, which the same boot exercised and which the unit test pins.

acceptance.criterion: A live bounded call on the installed harness proves the fixed path: an mpd_ulw / plan=false invocation returns a VALID result, evidenced from the harness session log (tool call + non-error result); if the live half cannot run, record a labelled `reported` entry with the reason — never a green

honestNotes: dist/** untouched by rule (out of scope, T-88): the SHIPPED packages/mpd-ulw-plugin/dist/index.js (sha256 24122dae82a78f8f…) still carries the RETIRED unconditional `planFile` return (measured, steps.shippedArtifacts.carriesRetiredUnconditionalPlanFile=true), so a boot of the shipped composition would still reproduce the defect. The schema-validity claim is a statement about the harness's validator as INSTALLED (measured: one scalar type per property, type arrays rejected) — if a future harness adds type-array support, the omission remains valid (planFile is not required), so the repair is forward-compatible either way.
